instruction_given_to_self: SEPARATE authoring pass, explicit spurious mindset. Reading the same round-3 slice, name 10 features that are plausibly PREDICTIVE but NOT quality, and that are FRESH -- none of the 22 channels already declared in rounds 1-2 (applied-domain framing, abstract length, branded name, enumerated formatting, LaTeX residue, resource magnitude, superlative density, dominant topic, benchmark name-dropping, anonymised-repo boilerplate, industrial compute, belief-change genre, hedging density, priority claims, syntactic complexity, rhetorical questions, non-idiomatic English, acronym density, privacy/security subfield, first-person density, typographic emphasis, inline citations). Label-blind: `judgement` was never loaded; no criterion references acceptance or any outcome.
scale: 0-10 integer, NA if the abstract gives no evidence bearing on the criterion

criteria.name: Content-warning or ethics-disclaimer boilerplate
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how prominently the abstract carries a safety, content, or ethics disclaimer — a content warning, a harm advisory, a responsible-disclosure note. Score presence and prominence of the disclaimer only, not the ethics of the work.
criteria.rationale: Fresh channel. R3-DL57 opens verbatim with 'Content warning: This paper contains examples of harmful language and content.' Disclaimers are a venue-policy and era artefact — they became common only recently and are required for some tracks and not others.

criteria.name: Mathematical notation density in the abstract
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much formal mathematical notation appears in the abstract — inline symbols, variables, set or norm notation, complexity expressions, formulas. Score notational density only, not whether the mathematics is correct or deep.
criteria.rationale: Distinct from round-1 B04, which scored UNRENDERED markup residue; this scores legitimate, correctly-rendered notation load. R3-DH22 ($k$-HC$_2$, $p \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$), R3-DL47 ($\widetilde{O}(k^{-1/8})$), R3-DH20 ($\tilde{O}(\sqrt{T\ln T})$) versus notation-free abstracts such as R3-DH25 and R3-DL55. Notation conventions travel with subfield.

criteria.name: Density of percentage figures
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many percentage figures the abstract reports. Count percentage-formatted numbers only; do not judge whether they are impressive or well-supported.
criteria.rationale: Fresh, deliberately shallow counterpart to round-1 A03 (quantified headline vs a named baseline). R3-DH00 (six per-benchmark percentages), R3-DL38 (92.20%, ~50%), R3-DL57 (95%, 63.15%, 60%, 50%) versus percentage-free abstracts like R3-DH10 and R3-DH24. If the judge cannot separate counting percentages from evaluating evidence, the routing audit should catch it.

criteria.name: Enumeration of specific named models in a model zoo
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many specific named model checkpoints or product model names the abstract lists (for example particular sizes and variants of released models). Score the listing practice only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh and distinct from round-1 B08 (famous benchmark names) and B09 (industrial compute signals): this counts enumerated MODEL identifiers. R3-DH27 lists Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3-8B-1M, GLM-4-9B-1M, Yi-9B-200K, Phi-3-Mini-128K and Qwen2-7B-128K in one sentence; R3-DL44 names GPT-4o and Llama-3. Model-zoo enumeration is a publication-era convention.

criteria.name: Opens with a broad field-level platitude
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract's opening sentence is a generic statement about the field's importance or recent progress ('X has been widely used', 'X has made significant progress in recent years') rather than a statement specific to this work's problem. Score the opening move only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh discourse channel. R3-DH02 ('LSTM is one of the most widely used recurrent structures in sequence modeling'), R3-DH09 ('The learning-based video compression method has made significant progress in recent years'), R3-DL49 ('While current node classification methods for graphs have enabled significant progress'). Opening conventions are taught habits, not properties of the work.

criteria.name: Self-description as novel or new
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how often the abstract describes its own contribution with the words novel, new, or first-of-its-kind. Count the lexical self-description only; do not judge whether the work is actually novel.
criteria.rationale: A narrower lexical tic than round-1 B07 (general superlative density) and distinct from round-2 B19 (explicit priority claims, which assert being first). R3-DH04, R3-DH10, R3-DH17, R3-DL39 and R3-DL43 all self-describe as 'novel'. The bank already scores novelty substantively at items 79 and 88, so this isolates the word from the property.

criteria.name: Discourse-connective scaffolding density
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how heavily the abstract uses sentence-initial connectives to scaffold its argument — However, Moreover, Furthermore, Thus, Therefore, In contrast, Specifically. Score the connective density only.
criteria.rationale: Fresh register channel, distinct from round-2 B11 (sentence complexity) and B22 (first-person density). R3-DH03, R3-DH07 and R3-DL52 are heavily scaffolded; R3-DH11 and R3-DH25 much less so. Connective habits track writing training and subfield style.

criteria.name: A public repository URL appears in the abstract
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the abstract contains a real, public code or data link — a repository URL or hosted project address. Score 0 when there is no link. This is about a live public link, not about anonymised submission placeholders or promises to release later.
criteria.rationale: Deliberately the complement of round-1 B01, which scored anonymised-repo and release-on-acceptance boilerplate and came out ANTI-predictive (.478). R3-DL53 carries a github.com URL; R3-DL50 says weights and sampling code 'are available on GitHub'. Whether the two poles of the same artifact-availability channel carry opposite sign is worth measuring directly.

criteria.name: Explicit count-signalling of experimental scale
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract advertises the COUNT of its experiments — 'extensive experiments on six benchmarks', 'four datasets', 'across three tasks', 'comprehensive evaluations'. Score the advertising of counts only, not the actual breadth of the evaluation.
criteria.rationale: The shallow counterpart of round-1 A04 (breadth of evaluation actually enumerated), included as a paired probe: A04 was audited into the bank, so if this scores similarly the pair localises how much of A04's signal was mere count-advertising. R3-DH03 ('six visual benchmarks'), R3-DH21 ('4 real-world in-vivo datasets'), R3-DL48 ('four benchmark datasets').

criteria.name: Membership in the learning-theory / optimization subfield
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the abstract belongs to the learning-theory, optimization, or statistical-guarantees cluster — convergence rates, regret bounds, complexity results, estimator analysis. Score topic membership only; work of any quality in any other subfield scores 0.
criteria.rationale: A third fine-grained topic marker, after round-1 B05 (dominant topics) and round-2 B20 (privacy/security). Conspicuous on the dense-low side of this slice: R3-DL30 (early-stopping convergence), R3-DL39/40 (Additive Poisson Process), R3-DL47 (last-iterate NE convergence), R3-DL59 (JS-divergence variational inference) — while R3-DH22, R3-DH29 and R3-DH20 are also theory, which keeps the channel a genuine test rather than a giveaway.
